findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a step/AC that determines whether exit 127 was a power-cycle artifact or an entrypoint fault (inspect entrypoint + reproduce), and feed that into AC2's decision.

findings.finding: AC2 requires deciding restart-vs-fail-loud, but the 'Note on exit 127' states the crash cause is NOT established ('Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact... is NOT established'); the decision depends on info the plan flags as unresolved yet no AC resolves it.
scenarios: Executor must choose AC2's branch but cannot tell crash-loop from power-cycle artifact
findings.suggested_fix: Promote the exit-127 investigation from a note to a probe step whose outcome gates AC2's restart-vs-fail-loud choice.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] If AC2 chooses restart, require a bounded/backed-off restart with a max-attempts threshold after which it fails loudly, and instrument the restart attempts (metric/log).
evidence: AC2: 'silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode' — acknowledged but no bounded-retry mechanism required
findings.finding: AC2 introduces automatic restart behavior on a deployed long-running system but does not require a bounded-retry/backoff or crash-loop guard, only acknowledges the failure mode in prose.
scenarios: Service exits repeatedly; autodeploy restarts it every ~2 min forever
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: restart at most N times per window, then escalate to the loud-failure branch; emit a structured restart-attempt event.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, for the restart arm, the disposition on repeated failure: after N failed restarts within a window the condition becomes fatal/permanent and is reported loudly (not retried silently), and record why that threshold.
evidence: 'It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which; silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.'
Note on exit 127: '127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining, because those need different fixes.'
The plan flags the crash-loop hazard but never states the disposition when the restart arm's own attempt fails.
findings.finding: AC2 adds a new failure-handling arm (restart the dead service) but does not state its disposition contract: when the restart itself fails — e.g. the container is crash-looping and re-exits — the plan does not say, using an explicit disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent), what autodeploy then surfaces. AC2 asks to 'Decide and RECORD which' between restart and fail-loudly, but does not pin what disposition a FAILED restart yields.
scenarios: review-bot exits 127 on a genuine entrypoint fault; autodeploy restarts it, it re-exits, and the next run restarts again — an unbounded silent restart loop with no stated fatal/permanent disposition after N failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC2 an explicit disposition: a single failed start is transient/retryable; a service that re-exits within a bounded window (e.g. 3 restarts) is treated as fatal/crash-looping and surfaced loudly rather than restarted again.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify ownership/idempotency for the restart action: how overlapping autodeploy runs are serialized (or that a run observing a healthy container after its own restart no-ops), so the recovery is at-least-once-safe and reports remain unambiguous.
evidence: 'journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy (runs every ~2 min...)'
AC3: 'review-bot and opcert have a reconcile path, or a recorded reason they do not.'
The incident note cites 'a tracker write timing out under lock contention', showing lock/concurrency is live on this host — yet the restart action's own concurrency is unspecified.
findings.finding: Autodeploy runs every ~2 minutes and AC2/AC3 add a container-lifecycle mutation (restart of review-bot/opcert). The plan does not state ownership/concurrency for that mutation: whether overlapping or back-to-back runs can each issue a restart, and whether the restart action is idempotent so a second run observing a just-started container does not re-act. This is the CREATE/UPDATE ownership leg of a newly-introduced stateful reconcile path.
scenarios: Two autodeploy invocations near a run boundary both detect the same dead container and each issue docker start, double-starting or racing the recovery; or a run reports 'restarting' on a container the previous run already recovered, muddying the loud-vs-quiet signal AC5 relies on.

AC4: 'A liveness signal exists for the review bot such that its absence is detectable — today it is invisible'; the plan text edits only autodeploy behavior and names no publisher/alarm surface
findings.finding: AC4 requires a liveness signal whose ABSENCE is detectable, and AC1 requires autodeploy to 'say so', but the plan does not enumerate the two out-of-file consumers the codebase uses to make an autodeploy signal detectable: observability.sh (publish_autodeploy_marker_delta turns AUTODEPLOY_* journal markers into CloudWatch metrics) and monitoring_autodeploy.tf (the alarm on those metrics). A new dead-service marker/metric added only in autodeploy.sh would remain invisible without corresponding edits there.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC4/AC1 an explicit edit surface: emit an AUTODEPLOY_* marker for a declared-but-dead service, add a publish_autodeploy_marker_delta call in observability.sh, and a paired alarm in monitoring_autodeploy.tf (or justify a different detectability mechanism).

findings.finding: Autodeploy is a periodic reconciler (runs every ~2 min) that will now mutate shared host container state (restart) after a check-then-act ('is it down?' then 'start it'). The plan does not specify how concurrent/overlapping ticks or restart thrash are bounded — there is no restart budget, backoff, or ownership/lock discipline stated for the new restart path, so at-least-once (every-2-min) invocation could hammer a crash-looping container.

evidence: AC2: 'It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which; silently restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.'
'Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining, because those need different fixes.'
No AC uses an explicit disposition word (transient/retryable vs fatal/permanent) for the down-service arm.
findings.finding: AC2 defers the failure disposition ('Decide and RECORD which') without pinning, per arm, what autodeploy surfaces when a declared service is down: a transient/retryable condition (re-check next ~2-min tick) versus a fatal/permanent one (fail loudly / alert). The exit-127 note explicitly flags this ambiguity (power-cycle artifact = transient vs entrypoint fault = fatal) but the ACs never require the disposition to be expressed in retryable-vs-fatal terms.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' line to AC2: e.g. 'first observation of a declared-down service → transient, attempt N restarts with backoff; still down after budget → fatal, emit a distinct loud failure (not a no-op).'
